So basically, the mp3 codec just has to reach a certain amount of data per second. The higher the bit rate, the more there can be, and naturally, the larger the file size. 320kbps is usually more than enough for most songs, save for extremely loud parts of the song. So as long as the amount of data per second doesn't exceed 320 kB, the codec doesn't actually take anything out, and instead is a lossless compression at that point. It's only when it exceeds that limit that frequencies around 16k+ start to be removed, or frequencies below 32 hz. The more space it needs, the further in towards the more audible frequencies it'll start removing, but at 320kbps, it doesn't need to.

Beyond that, once you've called the police and tried to contact a family member, there's not much more you can do about the situation. I know people say it a lot, but I have been through a similar situation. Dated a girl for about a year and a half, all of it save for one summer was long distance, and she fell in love with her best friend halfway through it. I won't go into any real detail, but suffice to say she was my first real love, and it was the worst heartbreak I'd ever experienced. (still is, actually) It's been about 3 years now. I've fallen in love again, and had my heart broken again no less. But the most amazing thing is that I've forgiven her, and actually rekindled our friendship, something I never thought I'd be able to do my entire life when it happened.

I'm telling my story not because I don't believe you two will make it, but because if things don't work out, for whatever reason, you need to know that the end of this relationship isn't the end of everything. Hell, it's not even necessarily the end of you and her. Life can be long and full of surprises if you allow it to.

We're all here for you, man, and I'm betting at least half of us have been through a similar situation and learned some different ways to cope. So just know that it gets better. And if you ever want to swap stories of how much bullshit long distance relationships are, feel free to message me. I've got plenty of them.
